transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's been bringing you in to see me?

I guess… what finally pushed me to come in is work stuff. I’ll start follow-up items after audits or mentoring events, and I really do mean to finish them. But then a few days later I’ll realize the final email, or a review note, or some form just… never actually got done. It’s been happening enough that I’m worried about it.
Has this kind of difficulty finishing tasks and following through been a pattern for you since you were a kid or teenager, or is this something that's really only started recently?

No, it’s not really new. I mean… I remember it being on report cards even in elementary school. They’d say I was bright, but I lost assignments or missed little details, talked when I wasn’t supposed to, needed reminders to finish things.

My mom still brings up that I could do well on a test and then forget some project sitting in my backpack. So… yeah, it goes back pretty far.
Growing up, did you also tend to be really restless or fidgety, have trouble staying seated when you were supposed to, or find yourself blurting things out or interrupting people?

Yeah… I think so. Even now, in meetings, I’m usually tapping my foot under the table or clicking a pen. I shift around a lot. One coworker has joked she can hear my leg going, which was… embarrassing.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others mid-conversation, blurting out answers before someone finishes a question, or having trouble waiting your turn in line or in discussions?

Yeah… I do interrupt sometimes. Mostly in work conversations, especially with junior auditors. If I think I know the answer, it feels like it’s right there and kind of urgent, and I’ll jump in before they’re finished. I don’t always mean to.
Do you notice these same problems—like losing track of tasks, restlessness, or interrupting—affecting you outside of work too, like at home or in your personal relationships?

Yeah… it’s not just work.

At home, my husband has kind of taken over things like bills or commitments I said I’d handle, because I don’t always follow through reliably. I don’t love saying that, but it’s true.

And at work it’s gotten more noticeable too. There were mistakes and follow-up I didn’t finish that affected a client review, and… I worry people are wondering if I can really handle the promotion.
